title: Plan Ahead, Win Together: Development Fund Enhancements for 2027
author: VRobinson
text:
As we move into 2027, we're making meaningful changes to the SAP PartnerEdge program to help strengthen the role of SAP partners in delivering customer value, innovation, and business transformation. A key part of this includes new enhancements for the Development Fund – changes designed to reward partners who drive SAP's strategic priorities, while making the experience faster, simpler, and more predictable. Here’s what you can expect. 

 Alignment with SAP's Strategy 
 As we look to 2027, we’re deepening our commitment to partners who synergize their priorities with ours –doubling down on those driving SAP’s strategic focus areas of Public Cloud, Corporate, AI, and Net-New Customers. Partners pursuing net-new customer opportunities are strongly encouraged to register those deals early – deal registration signals intent, secures protection, and directly strengthens eligibility for Development Fund investments. 
 Importantly, this isn’t a new direction. The Public Cloud and Corporate mandate for the Development Fund already exists today, so there’s no need to change your strategy. This is about familiarity and building on what you already know. 
 What is changing is how closely alignment to these priorities shapes the support you receive . The more your Development Fund proposal aligns to these areas – including SAP’s AI strategy – the stronger your position. In short, the partners most aligned to SAP’s strategy are the ones we’ll invest in most. 
 The value exchange is simple: if you’re driving revenue for SAP in these areas, we’ll give you more predictability so you can plan with us. Let’s walk through what that looks like. 

 A Key Change: Greater Predictability Through Pre-Allocated Budgets 
 One of the most significant changes for 2027 is the introduction of pre-allocated budgets , designed to bring greater predictability to how partners plan their Development Fund activities. 
 This change is aimed at our partners driving the majority of SAP’s indirect revenue. For these partners, there’s less uncertainty around funding levels. Rather than wondering how much support might be available, you’ll have visibility into the budget within your allotment – at least for the first half of the year – and can propose against it. This means you can plan earlier and get off to a faster start in Q1. 
 You’ll still submit proposals and request against your budget, and the usual approval process still applies, but now there’s a defined number to plan against, giving you a stronger foundation for your planning. 

 Who Qualifies — and How Funding Is Calculated 
 Pre-allocated budgets are available to partners who reach $1M ACV in Corporate over the previous four rolling quarters (Q4 2025 through Q3 2026 at launch). Importantly, reaching the revenue threshold is just one part of qualifying – partners will still need to meet all entry, compliance, and eligibility criteria to receive a pre-allocated budget. 
 For eligible partners, the level of funding reflects both the scale of their business and how closely it aligns to SAP's strategic priorities. Two factors come into play: 
 Revenue above the threshold — the foundation of the allocation 
 Strategic multipliers — including percentage of Public Cloud business, Corporate focus, alignment to SAP’s AI strategy, and number of Net-New Names 
 In other words, the allocation grows in step with the scale and strategic focus of a partner’s business – so there’s real room to build on what you’ve already achieved. 

 For Partners Not Yet at This Level 
 If your business doesn't currently meet the threshold, it's important to know that you continue to have full access to Development Fund support. The only difference is that a budget isn't pre-allocated in advance. 
 The proposal process remains exactly as it is today: once you meet the entry, compliance, and eligibility criteria, you can request funds, share your business plan, and have your proposal assessed on its merits. Funding flows to the strongest proposals and business plans – so a compelling, well-aligned plan is always the key to success. 
 And, importantly, pre-allocated funds are just one part of a broader set of improvements. As you’ll see in the sections that follow, many of the 2027 changes are designed to benefit every partner, regardless of size or focus. 

 Simplifying the Partner Experience 
 For 2027, we're making the Development Fund easier to work with for every partner. 
 We're streamlining our forms and keeping the focus on what's genuinely used in the market. We're also reducing the number of questions in both the proposal and claims processes. 
 This comes directly from your feedback. We heard that the forms were asking too many questions, which led to errors and unnecessary back-and-forth. Our goal is simple: remove that friction so you can spend less time on paperwork and more time driving results. 

 Faster Payments and Smarter Processing 
 We're also investing in speed and automation to improve the experience from end to end. 
 Automated payments: Once a claim is approved, it flows directly through to payment – so you can expect reduced time to payment, starting with claims coming in at the end of Q1 2027. 
 AI-powered audit checks: Behind the scenes, automated checks help verify the documents you upload and speed up claim processing. You won't see this directly, but you'll feel it through faster reviews. 
 AI guidance on the front end: As you create proposals and submit claims, you'll receive helpful tips and support along the way to help you get it right the first time. 
 And this is just the beginning – we'll continue to improve these tools over time. 

 Prepare Now for 2027 Success 
 The 2027 Development Fund updates deliver three clear partner benefits: 
 Predictability — eligible partners know their budget up front and can plan ahead, execute faster in Q1, and request against a defined number 
 Simplicity — streamlined forms and fewer questions in both the proposal and claims processes 
 Speed — automated payments and smarter, AI-supported processing behind the scenes 
 Together, these reflect a single commitment: to invest most in the partners who invest in SAP’s strategic priorities— Public Cloud, Corporate, AI, and Net-New Customers —and to make that investment easier to access every step of the way. 
 If you haven’t already, now’s the time to double down on AI. With AI a major focus for the Development Fund, consider how your business plan can support SAP’s AI strategy. 
 Updated guides and a refreshed Development Fund page are available on SAP Partner Portal with the full details. Access these resources to start thinking now about how your business plan aligns to SAP’s 2027 priorities, so you’re ready to move the moment the new changes go live.

How to get notified for SAP Cloud Connector for newer version whenever released via Automation scripts 
 If we use BTP, SAP Cloud-Connector in our daily work, then this SAP Cloyd Connector version check process can be really useful. However with increased Cybersecurity attacks or Vulnerability, our clients might require us to keep checking newer updates available & apply the upgraded SAP Cloud Connector version. 

 Below points were kept in mind while setting up this process: 
 a) Also once we get alerted for 1 version, we don't need to get alerted again until we do the upgrade on the needed application 
 b) I set it independent of the system and this can be run on any Linux server, regardless whatever the version is installed on your server

title: Relembre a palestra: Entenda a nova apuração da CBS, do SAP ao Fisco #SITCWB2026
author: AdrianoCWB
text:
No dia 7 de novembro, no Auditório Gregor Mendel da PUCPR, Marcelo Diogo Passaglia, Diretor de Inovação da CHpro Solutions, apresentou no SAP Inside Track Curitiba 2026 a palestra "Entenda a nova apuração (CBS): do SAP ERP ao Fisco". 
 Sobre a palestra 
 A palestra partiu de uma pergunta que muitas empresas vão fazer: "A Receita calculou R$ 10 milhões. Eu simplesmente pago?". Marcelo mostrou o fluxo de apuração e recolhimento da CBS, em comparação com o do PIS/COFINS, e o cronograma do primeiro período, em janeiro de 2027: a apuração fica disponível em 15 de fevereiro de 2027, e o prazo de ajustes e o vencimento são em 26 de fevereiro de 2027. Ele lembrou que, se o contribuinte não se manifestar sobre a apuração assistida até o prazo, os valores são considerados confissão de dívida. 
 A mensagem central: a questão não é apenas "quanto devo?", mas "consigo explicar o valor?". 
 Situações do dia a dia que a palestra discutiu 
 Registrar a operação no ERP é diferente de acompanhar todo o seu ciclo fiscal. 
 Pagamento antecipado: com R$ 500 mil pagos, R$ 380 mil entregues em duas notas e R$ 120 mil de saldo em análise, quem acompanha o saldo até o fim da operação? 
 Multa, juros e perda de mercadoria no transporte têm regras diferentes e o mesmo desafio de acompanhamento. 
 Crédito de IBS e CBS identificado não significa crédito disponível para uso. 
 O recolhimento pelo adquirente (RAD) exige avaliar, decidir e acompanhar. É governança, não apenas gerar e pagar um documento. 
 O fornecedor também precisa saber se o cliente pagou o imposto por ele. 
 Para levar 
 Compras, faturamento e fiscal não precisam virar especialistas tributários. A tecnologia deve absorver a complexidade, orientar a etapa seguinte e deixar o fiscal governar as regras e decidir. 
 Antes: apurar, declarar, recolher. Agora: identificar, orientar, agir e confirmar. Como resumiu a palestra, o novo desafio não é apenas apurar, é operar o que foi apurado. 
 Sobre o palestrante e o patrocínio

title: Foreign Supplier Invoice Fails with "No EC Tax Number"? Fix the Tax Number Category
author: mohithgowdak
text:
If posting a supplier invoice for a vendor based in Norway, Switzerland, or Canada stops with a cryptic error about a missing EC tax number, the problem is almost certainly not on the invoice it is in a configuration table that nobody told you needed updating. 
 Picture the scenario: your accounts-payable team has just onboarded a new supplier from Norway. The business partner record looks complete, the purchase order is in place, and the goods have arrived. You open the Create Supplier Invoice app in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and the system refuses to post with the message: "Vendor master record has no EC tax number for country/region." 
 You stare at it for a moment. Nobody touched the tax number. The supplier exists in the system. The invoice data looks correct. What went wrong? The answer lies not in the invoice or the supplier record it lies in whether the system has ever been configured to hold a VAT registration number for that country in the first place. In this post, I want to unpack exactly why that error fires, walk through the three SSCUI steps that fix it, look at how the same pattern caught many teams off-guard after Brexit, and flag one gotcha that trips people up even after they think they have finished the fix. 
 What the error actually means 
 When you save a supplier invoice, the system runs a check called VAT_REGISTRATION_NUMBER_CHECK . This check looks for a valid tax or VAT registration number stored against the supplier's Business Partner record. To store that number, a tax number category for the supplier's country must already exist in configuration it acts as the slot that holds the value on the Business Partner. 
 If no category has been defined for that country, there is no slot, and therefore no number. The VAT_REGISTRATION_NUMBER_CHECK has nothing to verify, so it raises the error. The message references 'EC tax number' because the field type originally mapped to European Community VAT IDs, but the mechanism now covers tax registration numbers globally the terminology just stuck. 
 The key insight is this: the problem is a configuration gap, not a data quality problem. You cannot fix it by editing the Business Partner directly, because the field you need to populate does not yet exist for that country. You have to create it first. 
 The three-step fix using SSCUIs 
 The good news is that the fix involves no development work only two Self-Service Configuration UI (SSCUI) entries and a Business Partner update. Here is the sequence: 
 Define the tax number category. Open SSCUI 104758 "Define Tax Number Categories." Create the entry for the relevant country (for example, NO0 for Norway or CH0 for Switzerland) and assign the check rule VAT_REGISTRATION_NUMBER_CHECK to it. This is the step most people have never had to do before, because the categories for common countries are usually shipped pre-configured. Less common trading-partner countries are not. 
 Activate the category on the Business Partner. Open SSCUI 102415 "Maintain Tax Number Categories." Enable the category you just created. This step makes it visible as an option on Business Partner records without it, the category exists in the configuration table but is invisible at the transactional level. 
 Populate the supplier's tax number, then re-post. Navigate to the Business Partner for the affected supplier and enter the correct VAT or tax registration number under the newly available category. Save the Business Partner, then re-attempt the invoice posting. The VAT_REGISTRATION_NUMBER_CHECK now has a value to work with, and the invoice posts successfully. 
 KBA 3050306 - Vendor master record has no EC tax number for country &' error while using the App Create Supplier Invoice documents this resolution in detail and is the authoritative reference if you need step-by-step screenshots. 
 The same pattern in a Brexit context 
 If this scenario sounds familiar from a completely different situation, it may be because you encountered it after the United Kingdom left the European Union. At that point, the tax category GB6 the category used for UK Business Partners was absent from many systems. Consultants who went looking for a UK tax number field on the Business Partner simply could not find it. 
 The root cause was identical: a missing tax number category for a country. Nothing about the Business Partner data was wrong. The configuration slot did not exist. The fix followed exactly the same three-step pattern define GB6 in SSCUI 104758 , activate it in SSCUI 102415 , populate the Business Partner. KBA 3020913 Brexit: Tax Category GB6 is missing for Business Partner in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition documents the specifics. 
 What makes the Brexit case instructive is not the geography it is the mechanism. The same thing happens any time a country is new to your System: [SYSTEM], you acquire a supplier in a country you have never purchased from before, or a regulatory change creates a new category requirement. The error is always the same; the fix is always the same three steps. Recognising the pattern is what saves time. 
 A practical checklist for new country onboarding 
 Based on the pattern above, I now include this short checklist whenever I am helping a team onboard suppliers from a country that has not previously appeared in their system: 
 Verify tax number categories are defined for the new country in SSCUI 104758 before the first Business Partner is created. 
 Activate the categories in SSCUI 102415 defining without activating is the most common mistake. 
 Do a test Business Partner and confirm the tax number field is visible and saveable before the first live supplier is loaded. 
 Run a test invoice posting end-to-end not just a Business Partner check because the VAT_REGISTRATION_NUMBER_CHECK only fires during invoice posting, not during Business Partner save. 
 Document the categories you have added in your system documentation so the next person who onboards a supplier from that country does not have to diagnose this from scratch. 
 Further reading 
 KBA 3050306 Vendor master record has no EC tax number for country &' error while using the App Create Supplier Invoice 
 KBA 3020913 Brexit: Tax Category GB6 is missing for Business Partner in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 
 KBA 3759655 Tax Number Category Not Visible in Value Help of the Business Partner Master Data 
 Key takeaways 
 The 'Vendor master record has no EC tax number' error almost always points to a missing tax number category in configuration not a data problem on the supplier record. 
 Two SSCUIs are both required: define the category in SSCUI 104758 and activate it in SSCUI 102415 . Completing only one step leaves the supplier unable to store the VAT number. 
 The same root cause appeared after Brexit (category GB6 for UK) and will appear for any country not previously represented in your system. The fix is always the same three steps. 
 If the category does not appear in the Business Partner value help after activation, reopen the session do not assume the configuration failed. See KBA [PHONE] for details. 
 Add a 'verify tax number categories' step to your new-country onboarding checklist. Running it before the first supplier is loaded costs minutes; diagnosing it during an invoice backlog costs hours. 
 Has this error caught your team off-guard for a country not mentioned here? Drop a comment below knowing which country codes come up most in practice helps the whole community. And if you are building out the procure-to-pay process in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, explore the SAP Learning site for guided learning journeys on financial configuration and supplier invoice management.

title: Simplifying Everyday Planning Workflows with Key Data Entry Enhancements in SAP Analytics Cloud QRC4
author: johannes_huhn
text:
Introduction 
 Good news! The 2026 QRC4 release brings a wide range of useful product enhancements designed to make everyday planning and data entry faster, smoother, and more efficient. 
 Whether you're entering planning data, working with sheets, or managing your daily planning activities, these improvements aim streamline common workflows, and make the overall experience more intuitive and convenient. 
 In this blog post, we'll walk you through the key enhancements one by one, highlighting what's new, what has improved, and how you can benefit from these changes in your day-to-day planning activities. 

 Fluid Data Entry Performance Improvement 
 Over the past quarters and years, we have continuously strengthened and matured our Fluid Data Entry capabilities, making them robust and reliable. With the 2026 QRC4 release , we have taken another step forward by further optimizing performance. 
 In particular, this release significantly reduces the waiting time between a user's cell edit and the submission of the entered value for processing. In concrete terms, data entry submissions are now approximately one second faster than before. Please note that this performance improvement is available exclusively in Fluid Data Entry mode . 

 1) Data Entry: Insertion of multiple new lines 
 With the 2026 QRC4 release , SAP Analytics Cloud introduces a new data insertion mode for planning tables, making it easier to add multiple new lines in a single workflow. 
 This enhancement provides a flexible, spreadsheet-like editing experience in which users can freely enter, edit, and navigate through data before submitting their changes. In addition to manually entering data, users can also copy and paste data directly from Microsoft Excel or other external sources , including both master data and planning data. 
 In essence, this new functionality simplifies data entry, particularly when creating multiple new, previously unbooked member combinations or transferring larger amounts of rows from external sources into planning tables. 

 To access this new mode, simply right-click a table cell and select "Add Member Combinations" from the context menu. This opens the new data entry interface, which offers several useful capabilities: 

 Flexible data entry and pasting: Enter multiple new lines manually or paste data directly from the clipboard, including master data and planning data. 

 Automatic data validation: Entered values, such as master data members, are automatically validated to help ensure data consistency. 

 Clear error highlighting: Invalid values are highlighted, allowing users to quickly identify and correct issues before submitting their changes. 

 Controlled data submission: Once all entries have been reviewed, users can click the "Process Data" button to submit their changes for processing. 
 By combining flexible data entry, clipboard integration, and built-in validation, this new mode makes creating multiple planning entries more convenient. 
 2) Data Entry: Reposting Planning Data 
 For users who frequently need to move planning data from one member to another, the 2026 QRC4 release brings a welcome enhancement: Repost . 
 Similar to a traditional cut-and-paste operation, Repost allows users to move planning data from one member combination to another through a single, intuitive interaction. Instead of manually adjusting values across multiple cells, users can easily reassign existing planning data. Typical use cases include reassigning cost center budgets, moving budgets between WBS elements, transferring quantities between sales channels , and many other scenarios where planning data needs to be redistributed or reassigned. 
 The new Repost functionality is easily accessible directly within planning tables. Users can simply double-click a master data cell or right-click the cell to access the corresponding Repost option. 
 In addition, story designers can further tailor the Repost experience to targeted requirements. For example, they can configure the context of a Repost operation to exclude actual data or focus on specific measures available in the table. 

 3) Data Entry: Paste Special – Respect Target Cell Scaling 
 With the 2026 QRC4 release , SAP Analytics Cloud introduces a new Paste Special option: Respect Scale of Target Cell . This enhancement gives users greater flexibility and control over how pasted values are interpreted and processed. 
 Previously, pasting data into a planning table always submitted the original, unscaled values from the source. For example, copying a value of 100 from Excel would result in a value of 100 being submitted, regardless of whether the target cell was displayed in units, thousands, or millions. 
 With the new option, users can choose to respect the scaling of the target cell when pasting data. This means that pasted values are interpreted according to the scale configured in the target cell. For example, when pasting a value of 100 into a cell displayed in thousands, the system interprets the value as 100.000. 
 Users can now choose between pasting the original, unscaled values or respecting the target cell's scaling 

 4) Data Entry: Customizable Cell Highlighting Colors (Planned for 2027 QRC1) 
 For planning users, the familiar blue and yellow cell highlighting colors have long been an integral part of the data entry experience in SAP Analytics Cloud. These colors provide immediate visual feedback on the status of entered values: blue indicates that a data entry has not yet been processed, while yellow confirms that the data has been processed . 
 With the upcoming 2027 QRC1 release , we plan to introduce additional theming capabilities that will give story designers greater flexibility in customizing these highlighting colors. 
 Specifically, story designers will be able to configure the highlighting colors for both the in-processing and processed states , allowing them to better align the data entry experience with their corporate's visual design and users expectations. 
 In addition to choosing custom colors, designers will also have the option to set either highlighting state to transparent . This makes it possible to display both states, highlight only one of them, or remove highlighting altogether. For example, by setting the current blue highlighting color to transparent, users would only see cells highlighted once their data entries have been processed. This can be particularly useful in planning tables where data entry processing is already very fast. 
 Note: This enhancement is currently planned for 2027 QRC1 .

title: Relembre a palestra: S/4HANA na Prática, do Upgrade à Reforma Tributária #SITCWB2026
author: AdrianoCWB
text:
No dia 7 de novembro, no Auditório Gregor Mendel da PUCPR, Paulo Kanofre, Coordenador de Operações SAP, e Gilson Bormann, Especialista em Desenvolvimento e Arquitetura de Soluções SAP, da Vexper Consulting, apresentaram no SAP Inside Track Curitiba 2026 a palestra "S/4HANA na Prática: Do Upgrade à Reforma Tributária". 
 Upgrade do S/4HANA, passo a passo 
 A estratégia do upgrade cabe em três ideias: criar um ambiente novo a partir de uma cópia da produção, fazer o upgrade nessa cópia e só então seguir para o QAS e o PRD, e manter uma rota de emergência entre DEV e PRD. A síntese usada na palestra: primeiro a cópia, depois o QAS, só então o PRD. 
 Passo 1: cria-se o ambiente DEV_2 a partir de uma cópia do PRD. 
 Passo 2: o upgrade acontece primeiro no DEV_2, sem tocar na produção. 
 Passo 3: o upgrade segue para o QA. 
 Passo 4: as correções e programas do DEV_2 viajam por transporte até o QA, para que o que já foi resolvido não seja descoberto de novo.

 Passo 7: após o go-live, um time de suporte pró-ativo acompanha a virada para corrigir na hora qualquer falha não prevista.

title: Life-Time Events of Purchase Orders and Their Effect on Accruals
author: Balazs_Szauder
text:
Time-Dependency in the Accrual Engine versus Time-Independency of Purchase Order Data 
 Purchase Order Time-Independency 
 Purchase orders are time-independent : All changes made by users (e.g., via transaction ME22N) are valid immediately for all times 
 Changes overwrite the original value in the purchase order 
 Users do not need to enter a date for when changes become valid 
 Accrual Object Time-Dependency 
 Accrual objects in the Accrual Engine are time-dependent : Users must enter a date from which each change becomes valid 
 Reason for time-dependency : Accrual objects generally represent contract-like data, and contracts can be time-dependent 
 Purchase Order Accruals Application 
 Accrual objects can be created for purchase orders 
 Changes to purchase order data trigger corresponding accrual object changes 
 Example : Changing the net price in a purchase order item requires adjustment of the total amount to be accrued in the accrual subobject 
 Automatic Date Determination 
 When users maintain purchase orders (e.g., transaction ME22N), they cannot enter a date for change validity 
 The system automatically determines a reasonable date from which the change becomes valid in the accrual object 
 This date determination logic is hard-coded in the system 

 1. Create or Delete PO Items 

 Events Influencing Accrual Amounts in the Accrual Engine for Purchase Orders: 
 Creation of the Purchase Order 
 Customizing determination : The Purchase Order Accruals application customizing determines whether an accrual object will be created 
 Status requirement : The purchase order must have a suitable status 
 Time-independency : The new purchase order is created in the Accrual Engine as time-independent (table ACESOBJ) 
 Creation of a New Purchase Order Item 
 Customizing determination : The Purchase Order Accruals application customizing determines whether an accrual subobject will be created 
 Account assignment handling : For each account assignment given in a purchase order item, a separate accrual subobject will be created 
 Accrual item creation : The customizing of the Purchase Order Accruals application determines: 
 Which accrual items are created 
 Which algorithms they use to calculate and post the periodic accrual amounts 
 Technical validity period : The new purchase order item is created in the Accrual Engine to be technically valid all time: from 01.01.0001 until 31.12.9999 (table ACESOBJ_ITEM, fields LIFE_START_DATE and LIFE_END_DATE) 
 Deletion of an Existing Purchase Order Item 
 Deletion restriction : Once a purchase order item is created and saved, it cannot be deleted 
 Alternative action : Users can mark the item as to be deleted (EKPO-LOEKZ) 
 Posted accruals constraint : If accruals have already been posted, the accrual subobject cannot be deleted any more 
 Status change : The status of the accrual items of the corresponding accrual subobject will be set to Obsolete 
 Accrual consequence : Accruals will be set to zero as a consequence in future fiscal periods 
 Retroactive validity : This change is valid in the Accrual Engine for all time, including former periods 

 2. Change PO Item 

 Changes of an Existing Purchase Order Item That Affect Accruals 
 Accrual Method Dependency 
 Algorithm-dependent impact : Whether changes in the purchase order affect accruals depends on the accrual method, that is, on the accrual calculation algorithm 
 Customer-programmed algorithms : Since the algorithms can be programmed by the Customer, it is not possible to provide a complete list of changes that will affect the accruals 
 Three-Step Approach Impact 
 Formula : Accruals = plan minus actual 
 Change scope : All changes in the purchase order (item) that affect the planned costs will affect the accruals 
 Replicated Data from Purchase Order to Accrual Engine 
 Only few data are replicated by the system from the purchase order (item) into the Accrual Engine: 
 Total planned costs 
 Start of Life date and End of Life date : Determined during the replication; these dates determine the date interval between which the costs are planned to be accrued 
 Impact of Changes on Replicated Data 
 Update trigger : Changes in the purchase order (item) that affect the replicated data will lead to an update in the accrual subobject 
 Temporal validity : These changes are valid in the Accrual Engine for all time, that is, from 01.01.0001 until 31.12.9999 (table ACESOBJ_ITEM, fields LIFE_START_DATE and LIFE_END_DATE) 

 Changes of an Existing Purchase Order Item That Affect Accruals (Three-Step Approach) 
 Changing the Delivery Schedule 
 Changing delivery date or quantity in existing entries 
 Source: Transaction ME23N 
 Impact: Affects the total planned costs and/or the life time 

 Creating a new entry in the delivery schedule (or deleting an existing one) 
 Impact: Affects the total planned costs and/or the life time 
 Changing the Net Price in the Purchase Order Item 
 Impact: Affects the total planned costs 

 Changing the Item Category of a PO Item 
 Example : From Standard to Limit 
 Consequence : Can lead to different accrual item types and methods 
 Determination source : Due to the Customizing in IMG activity "Define Accrual Item Types and Methods for MM Purchase Order Items" (transaction ACEIMG) 
 Reference : See separate slide for details 
 Adding a New Account Assignment 
 Structural impact : Leads to a split of the accrual subobject into two subobjects 
 New subobject creation : The new accrual subobject is created in the Accrual Engine to be technically valid all time, that is, from 01.01.0001 until 31.12.9999 (table ACESOBJ_ITEM, fields LIFE_START_DATE and LIFE_END_DATE) 

 Accrual Method PLN_LIND_P Overview 
 Method name : Planned costs with linear distribution 
 Functionality : This method distributes the total amount of the accrual subobject linearly between the Start of Life and End of Life date that is given in the accrual subobject 
 Changes Affecting Accruals 
 Changes in Total Amount 
 Impact : Changes in the purchase order that change the total amount of the purchase order item will lead to different accruals 
 Example : Changing the net price of the purchase order item in transaction ME22N 
 Changes in Service Period (Lean Services) 
 Applicable scenario : The method PLN_LIND_P can be used for purchase order items that represent a Lean Service 
 Date entry capability : In Lean Services, the user can enter a Start Date and End Date in the purchase order item between which the service is planned to be received from the supplier 
 Date replication : These dates are replicated into the accrual subobject as Start of Life and End of Life 
 Consequence : Changing the start or end date in the purchase order item in transaction ME22N will affect the accruals 
 Definition of Lean Services 
 Identification criterion : Lean Services means that in the purchase order item, the field Product Type Group has the value 2. 

 3. Set Delivery Complete Indicator in PO Item 

 Overview of Delivery Complete Indicator 
 Purpose : Setting the indicator Delivery Complete in the purchase order item signals that no further goods receipts or costs are expected 
 Goods Receipt and Accounting Posting 
 Posting mechanism : If valuated goods receipts are posted for a purchase order item, these goods receipts post the costs in Accounting 
 Accrual relevance : Since accruals are usually posted for costs that are expected for future fiscal periods, no accruals are required as soon as the last goods receipt was posted 

 Effect on Accrual Amounts 
 Requirement : As soon as a user has set the indicator Delivery Complete in the purchase order item, the accrual amount for the future fiscal periods must be zero 
 Note on timing : What "future" exactly means in this case will be explained 
 Conditions for Accounting Posting 
 If the following conditions are met, the goods receipt will perform a posting in Accounting: 
 a) The indicator Goods receipt is true AND 
 b) The indicator GR non-valuated is false 
 Cost posting : If the purchasing document item has an account assignment like cost center, then costs will be posted 
 Manual Setting of Delivery Complete Indicator 
 User action : The indicator Deliv. Compl. (=Delivery Complete) in the purchase order item is set manually by a user 
 Meaning : If it is set, then this means that no further goods receipt, that is, no further costs, is expected: No accruals are needed any more 

 Time-Independence of Delivery Complete Indicator 
 User capability : In the purchase order item, a user can set the indicator Delivery Complete 
 Time-independent characteristic : This indicator is time-independent 
 Information limitation : The purchase order item does not store the information from which date onwards this indicator is valid 
 Accrual Calculation Effect 
 Accrual amount requirement : For the accrual calculation, setting this final indicator means that the accrual amount must be = 0 after the posting date of the final goods receipt 
 Pre-posting period accruals : Before this posting date, still goods receipts are expected – and as a consequence potentially accruals are required 

 For System Process to Achieve Zero Accruals After Delivery Complete is Set, please refer to the KBA 0003803785 

 4. Set Final Invoice Indicator in PO Item 

 Setting the Final Invoice Indicator in PO Items 
 Scenario with No Valuated Goods Receipts: When no valuated goods receipts are posted for a purchase order item, supplier invoices directly post costs to Accounting. 
 Purpose of Accruals: Accruals are typically posted for costs expected in future fiscal periods. Once the last invoice is posted, accruals are no longer needed. 
 Setting the Final Invoice Indicator: The "Final Invoice" indicator in the purchase order item is set either: 
 Manually by a user, or 
 Automatically during posting of the final invoice 
 Effect of Final Invoice Indicator: When the indicator is set, it signifies that: 
 No further supplier invoices are expected 
 No further costs are expected 
 No accruals are needed anymore 
 The accrual amount for all future fiscal periods must be reduced to zero 
 The specific meaning of "future" in this context will be explained in subsequent documentation 
 Functional Equivalence: The "Final Invoice" indicator (used when there are no valuated goods receipts) produces the same effect for accruals as the "Delivery Complete" indicator (used when there are valuated goods receipts) - both signal that no further accruals should be posted for the purchase order item. 

 Time-Independent Nature of Final Invoice Indicator 
 Indicator Characteristics: 
 A user can set the "Final Invoice" indicator in the purchase order item 
 This indicator is time-independent 
 The purchase order item does not store information about the date from which the indicator becomes valid 
 Effect on Accrual Calculation 
 Accrual Amount Requirements: 
 After the posting date of the final goods receipt, the accrual amount must equal zero 
 Before this posting date, goods receipts may still be expected 
 Consequently, accruals may still be required before the final goods receipt posting date 
 System Steps to Achieve Zero Accruals After Final Invoice Indicator is Set 
 Step 1: Replication into Accrual Engine 
 During replication of the purchase order into the Accrual Engine 
 If the "Final Invoice" indicator is true in the purchase order item 
 The system changes the status of the accrual subobject to "Prematurely Finished" (status "F") 
 Step 2: Saving the Posting Date 
 The system saves the posting date of the final invoice in the accrual subobject 
 This is stored in the field "Premature Finish Date" 
 This approach ensures that after the posting date of the final invoice, posted accruals will be released 
 Step 3: Release Posting 
 The next accrual posting run will perform a release posting 
 This release posting results in an accruals balance of zero 

 Alternative Approach 
 If Three-Step

title: 4 Step: Determine Accrual Item Types and Accrual Methods
author: Ujhelyi_Zsuzsi
text:
After determining the accrual classification and lifetime for the purchase order item (Step 2), the system proceeds to identify the accrual item types and accrual methods required by the Accrual Engine to compute the accrual amounts for each period. 
 Accrual Item Type : Represents a specific amount to be calculated by the Accrual Engine. It serves as the key field for an accrual item within the accrual subobject. 
 Accrual Method : Defines the algorithm used to calculate the amount for a given accrual item type. It functions as an attribute of the accrual item within the accrual subobject. 
 Screen-shot of transaction POACTREE03: The accrual items and their methods that were created as part of the accrual subobject for the purchase order item. 

 Customizing: List Screen 

 After the PO item was classified, the accrual item types and accrual methods are derived based on the table entries in Customizing activity Define Accrual Item Types and Methods for MM Purchase Order Items -> Define accrual item type and method based on PO item. 

 Detail Screen 
 Although three accrual item types can be defined, the user only enters the Accruals item type in this screen. The other two item types— Planned Costs and Actual Costs —are automatically populated if the three-step approach is used (i.e., if the accrual item types for planned and actual costs are assigned in the Customizing activity Define Accrual Item Types ). 
 If no relationships are defined (meaning the three-step approach is not used), the system will only use the Accruals item type. In this case, you must implement a customer-defined accrual method that calculates the accrual amount using a custom algorithm. 
 Recommended Approach: Use the three-step method (where Accruals = Planned Costs – Actual Costs ). 

 The user enters only ACCRL: The other accrual item types PLNCST and ACTCST are taken automatically from the settings in Cust. activity Define Accrual Item Types 

 Planned and Actual Costs 
 In the example shown in the screen-shot in the last slide, the three-step approach is used, that is, an accrual item type for planned costs and an accrual item type for actual costs are assigned to the Accruals accrual item type 

 Detail Screen: Accrual Method for ACCRL 
 Accrual Item Types and Methods 
 While the system automatically determines the accrual item types for planned and actual costs based on the Accruals (ACCRL) type, users must manually specify the accrual methods for all applicable accrual item types. 
 Three-Step Approach Rule: 
 For the Accruals (ACCRL) item type (as shown in the screenshot below), always use the PLN-ACT accrual method. This method calculates the difference between planned and actual costs: 
 Planned Costs – Actual Costs 
 If the result is negative, it defaults to zero (since accruals cannot be negative). 
 For further details, refer to the corresponding slides on the PLN-ACT accrual method. 

 Detail Screen: Accrual Method for ACTCST 
 In the three-step approach, you can use the accrual method ACT_COSTS for the Actual Costs item type (here: ACTCST): – This method determines the actual costs that have already been posted (up to a given date) for the purchase order item/accnt. Assignment. For details see corresponding slides for this accrual method 

 Detail Screen: Accrual Method for PLNCST 
 When configuring the Planned Costs accrual item type (e.g., PLNCST ), you must select an accrual method that aligns with the accrual classification. Below is the recommended method for the SDELS classification: 
 Accrual Classification: SDELS (Planned costs according to delivery schedule) 
 Recommended Accrual Method: PLN_DELSCH 
 This method calculates planned costs by analyzing the delivery dates and quantities specified in the purchase order (PO) item’s delivery schedule. 

 For SPERP (Planned Costs linearized between start and end date) , you can use the accrual method PLN_LIND_P for the Planned Costs accrual item type (e.g., PLNCST ). 
 Key Features of PLN_LIND_P: 
 This method calculates planned costs by linearly distributing the total net amount of the PO item between a defined start and end date . 
 For Lean Services , the start and end dates are automatically derived from the PO item. 

 Key Use Case for Customer-Defined Accrual Classifications (e.g., Z0001): Customer-defined classifications allow for customized planned cost calculations that differ from the system’s default behavior for standard classifications like SDELS and SPERP . 
 Example: You may want planned costs to follow a linear distribution between a defined start and end date—even if Lean Services are not in use. 
 Important Note: 
 Customer-specific classifications (e.g., Z001 ) and the associated start/end dates must be determined via the BAdI method: IF_BADI_POAC_MMPO_2_ACE_TRANSF>DET_POITEM_ACCR_CLASSIFICATION

title: Step 3: Lifetime of an Accrual Subobjects
author: Ujhelyi_Zsuzsi
text:
Purpose 
 Accrual Subobject Lifetime Each accrual subobject in the Accrual Engine has a defined lifetime, determined by the Start of Life and End of Life date fields. 
 This lifetime is particularly important when periodic accrual amounts are calculated by linearizing the total PO item amount over time. By definition, the linearization period aligns with the accrual subobject’s lifetime. 
 How it is determined 
 When a purchase order (PO) is transferred into the Accrual Engine, the system calculates the lifetime of the accrual subobject based on the dates provided in the PO. The lifetime is then stored in the accrual subobject. The following cases apply: 
 1. Accruals Based on Delivery Schedule (SDELS Classification) 
 If the accrual classification is SDELS, the system evaluates the first and last delivery dates to determine the lifetime. 
 Exceptions: 
 · If the first delivery date is in the future, the Start of Life (SoL) date defaults to the PO creation date (field EKKO-BEDAT – Purchasing Document Date). 
 · For item category E (Enhanced Limit), the user can manually enter a Start Date and End Date in the PO item. These dates are used as the Start of Life (SoL) and End of Life (EoL), similar to Lean Services. 
 2. Linearized Accruals Between Start and End Dates (SPERP Classification) 
 By default, this applies only to Lean Services (accrual classification SPERP). The system uses the Start Date and End Date from the PO item as the lifetime. 
 3. Custom Accrual Classifications (e.g., Z0001) 
 If the customer defines a custom accrual classification (e.g., Z0001), the lifetime must be determined via the BAdI: 
 · BADI_POAC_MMPO_2_ACE_TRANSFER 
 · Method: IF_BADI_POAC_MMPO_2_ACE_TRANSF->DET_POITEM_ACCR_CLASSIFICATION

title: Step 2: Transfer of Purchase Orders into the Accrual Engine: Classify Purchase Order items
author: Ujhelyi_Zsuzsi
text:
Accrual Classification Process 
 After a purchase order item is selected, the system follows a two-step process to determine and classify accruals: 
 1. Initial Assessment – The system first evaluates whether accruals will likely be required for the purchase order item. 
 2. Accrual Classification – In the second step, the system classifies the purchase order item based on accrual requirements. 
 Key Determinations in Accrual Classification: 
 · The classification dictates the algorithm used to calculate accruals for each period. 
 · The system also establishes the lifetime of the purchase order, defining a start date and end date—accruals are calculated within this timeframe. 
 · The accrual item types and accrual methods are determined by: 
 o The accrual classification 
 1. Default Accrual Classifications for Purchase Order Items 
 The system provides two predefined accrual classifications for purchase order items: 
 · SDELS – Lifetime dates derived from the delivery schedule 
 · SPERP – Lifetime dates derived from the performance period 
 These values are part of the SAP standard delivery and cannot be modified by customers. 
 For further details, refer to the IMG activity Define Purchase Order Item Accrual Classifications (view V_TPOAC_ACRCLASS). 
 SPERP 
 Classification Value SPERP The system uses the classification value SPERP for purchase order items that represent either a Lean Service or an Enhanced Limit. 
 Lean Services For Lean Services, the Product Type Group of the purchase order item is set to 2. In such cases, users can manually enter a start date and end date in the purchase order item (via transaction ME22N). These dates define the period during which the service is expected to be received from the supplier. 
 Cost Calculation for SPERP Items If a purchase order item is classified as SPERP, the system (using default customizing) will calculate the planned costs by linearizing the total amount of the purchase order item across the specified start and end dates. 
 o The purchase order type 
 o The purchase order item category 
 SDELS 
 Classification Value SDELS The system uses SDELS as the default classification value for purchase order items. 
 Exceptions to Default Classification A different classification value is applied only if: 
 · The purchase order item involves the procurement of a Lean Service, or 
 · The BAdI method IF_BADI_POAC_MMPO_2_ACE_TRANSF->DET_POITEM_ACCR_CLASSIFICATION returns a custom classification value (e.g., Z001 or Z002). 
 Planned Cost Calculation for SDELS Classification If a purchase order item is classified as SDELS, the system (using default customizing) calculates planned costs by evaluating the delivery dates in the purchase order item’s delivery schedule. The planned costs for each delivery date are determined based on: 
 · The quantity of the delivery schedule entry, and 
 · The net price specified in the purchase order item. 
 2. Customer-Defined Purchase Order Item Accrual Classifications 
 Potential Use Cases Beyond Predefined Accrual Classifications 
 There may be scenarios where the predefined accrual classifications (SDELS and SPERP) do not meet specific business requirements. 
 Example: Accruals may need to be calculated using linearization between a start and end date, even when the purchase order item does not represent a Lean Service. In such cases, the system lacks predefined logic to determine the applicable start and end dates. Instead, the start date must be derived from a custom field (e.g., ZSTART_DATE in the purchase order item table EKPO). 
 Implementation Considerations: To support this custom accrual logic, several extension activities are required. 
 See note 2888110 for more details. 
 Customizing Accrual Item Types and Methods for MM Purchase Order Items 
 Objective: Define accrual item types and methods based on PO item attributes to ensure proper accrual calculation. 
 Steps: 
 1. Navigate to the Customizing Activity: 
 o Path: Define Accrual Item Types and Methods for MM Purchase Order Items → Define accrual item type and method based on PO item. 
 2. Create Entries for Relevant Combinations: 
 o For each applicable combination of: 
 § Purchasing Document Type 
 § Item Category 
 Z0001) 
 o Specify the following: 
 § Accrual Item Types (e.g., accrual, planned costs, actual costs) 
 § Accrual Methods (to be used for accrual calculation) 
 3. System Behavior: 
 o When an accrual subobject is created for a PO item matching the defined combination (Document Type + Item Category + Accrual Classification), the system will automatically apply the configured accrual item types and methods. 
 Note: 
 · The accrual classification is determined by the BAdI BADI_POAC_MMPO_2_ACE_TRANSFER

title: Step 1: Transfer of Purchase Orders into the Accrual Engine
author: Ujhelyi_Zsuzsi
text:
Excluded Purchase Order Items: Selection 
 Exclusion Criteria for Accrual Object Creation 
 Accrual objects should not be created for the following purchase order (PO) items: 
 1. Purchases for Stock (EKPO-KZVBR = ) 
 o No accruals are required since these items do not incur costs. 
 2. Fixed Asset Purchases (EKPO-KZVBR = A) 
 o Accruals are unnecessary for fixed asset acquisitions. 
 3. Inter-Company Stock Transfers (EKKO-BSAKZ = T) 
 o These transactions involve internal transfers rather than external suppliers, eliminating the need for accruals. 
 Handling Changes to PO Items 
 A PO item’s attributes (e.g., account assignment category) can be modified (e.g., via transaction ME22N), which may affect accrual processing. For example: 
 · A user initially creates a PO item with account assignment category = K (cost center), setting EKPO-KZVBR = V. 
 · The item is transferred to the Accrual Engine. 
 · Later, the user changes the account assignment to A (fixed asset), updating EKPO-KZVBR = A. 
 In such cases: 
 · The transaction POAC_MM2ACE_TRANSFER must still select the PO item (even if KZVBR = A) to update the existing accrual subobject. 
 · The accrual items should be marked as obsolete to reflect the change. 
 · Note: If a PO item originally had KZVBR = A, no accrual subobject will be created. 
 PO Document Type and Item Category 
 Customizing Activity: Define Accrual Item Types and Methods for MM Purchase Order Items 
 In this customizing activity, you specify which purchase order items are subject to accrual processing. Key steps include: 
 1. Define Accrual Item Type and Method Based on PO Item 
 o Create entries for combinations of Purchasing Document Type and Purchasing Document Item Category. 
 o These entries determine which purchase order items are eligible for accruals. 
 2. System Behavior 
 o The system generates an accrual subobject for a purchase order item only if a corresponding entry exists in this customizing table. 
 o If no entry is found for the document type and item category, the system will not create an accrual subobject. Consequently: 
 - No accruals will be calculated. 
 - No accrual postings will be made for that purchase order item. 

 Only for combinations of PO Document Type and PO Item Category that are entered here, accrual objects will be created; this way you can restrict the scope of the accruals solution, for example 

 Thresholds for Purchase Order Item Values 
 Customizing Activity: Define Accrual Item Types and Methods for MM Purchase Order Items 
 In this customizing activity, you can define a threshold amount to exclude "small" purchase order items from accrual processing. 
 Key Steps: 
 1. Navigate to the section: Define accrual item type and method based on PO item. 
 2. Set the threshold amount for the PO item net value to determine which items should be excluded from accrual. 
 3. Use the F1 help for detailed guidance on this field.

title: Stop Fetching a CSRF Token for Every Call: How I Cached Tokens and Auto-Healed Expiry in SAP CPI
author: Sakshe
text: Every message from our third-party system made CPI fetch a brand-new CSRF token before posting to SAP ECC. 100 messages meant 200 calls. A timer-based refresh didn't help either, because tokens expired after 20 minutes, sometimes 35, never the promised 60. This blog shows the pattern I built: cache the token in a Data Store, refresh it on a schedule, and let the iFlow repair itself when ECC says "token expired". The sender never sees a failure.

title: KI-Governance im öffentlichen Sektor: Wie Behörden Kontrolle und Automatisierung in Einklang bringen
author: AnnikaSchlueter
text:
Die Diskussion über KI in der öffentlichen Verwaltung dreht sich oft um die falsche Frage. Nicht „Können wir KI einsetzen?" ist das Problem. Sondern: „Wie stellen wir sicher, dass wir wissen, was unsere KI-Agenten tun und dass wir jederzeit Rechenschaft darüber ablegen können?" 
 Das ist keine rhetorische Frage. Für Behörden hat sie handfeste rechtliche Konsequenzen: EU AI Act, Begründungspflicht im Verwaltungsverfahren, Anforderungen aus dem Datenschutz. Wer KI in Verwaltungsprozessen einsetzt, ohne Governance von Anfang an mitzudenken, baut auf Sand. 
 In einem Demo-Szenario, dem Forderungsmanagement einer öffentlichen Verwaltung, haben wir gezeigt, wie ein vollständiger, geschlossener Kreislauf aus Identifikation, Automatisierung und Kontrolle in der Praxis aussieht. Was dabei entstanden ist, ist kein Pilotprojekt für übermorgen. Es ist ein Modell, das heute funktioniert und auf jeden Verwaltungsprozess übertragbar ist. 
 Schritt 1: Erst verstehen, wo KI wirklich hilft 

 Bevor überhaupt ein KI-Agent ins Spiel kommt, steht eine nüchterne Analyse: Wo verliert der Prozess aktuell Zeit? Und wo wäre Automatisierung sinnvoll und nicht nur technisch möglich? 
 Der Process Consulting Agent von SAP Signavio beantwortet genau diese Frage. Er analysiert Prozessdaten in natürlicher Sprache, identifiziert Engpässe und bewertet, welche Prozessschritte das größte Automatisierungspotenzial haben. In unserem Szenario war die Empfehlung eindeutig: Der Schritt „Stundungsantrag prüfen" im Forderungsprozess ist regelbasiert, wiederkehrend und blockiert den gesamten nachgelagerten Ablauf. 
 Für die Verwaltungsleitung ist das ein entscheidender Schritt: kein Bauchgefühl, kein internes Überzeugungsarbeit ohne Datenbasis. Sondern eine belegbare Grundlage dafür, warum KI an genau dieser Stelle Sinn ergibt und wie hoch der erwartete Mehrwert ist. 
 Schritt 2: Den Prozess sehen, wie er wirklich ist 

 Empfehlungen brauchen Beweise. Das Process Intelligence Dashboard von SAP Signavio liefert genau das: eine Visualisierung des Forderungsprozesses, wie er tatsächlich abläuft. 
 Das Ergebnis ist sofort lesbar: Der Schritt „Stundungsantrag prüfen" ist der größte Flaschenhals im gesamten Ablauf. Die Durchlaufzeit liegt weit über dem Zielwert. Und weil dieser Schritt mitten im Prozess sitzt, verzögert er alles, was danach kommt: die Bescheiderstellung, die Buchung, den Abschluss des Falls. 
 Das ist der Moment, in dem aus einer Vermutung eine Entscheidungsgrundlage wird. Und in dem klar wird: Hier nicht zu automatisieren hat einen Preis: in Zeit, in Personalkapazität, in Bürger:innenzufriedenheit. 
 Schritt 3: Den Agenten bauen mit dem Wissen der Verwaltung 

 Mit dieser Grundlage geht es in Joule Studio . Hier entsteht der KI-Agent, der den Prüfungsschritt übernimmt. In einem Low-Code-Werkzeug, das Fachbereich und IT gemeinsam nutzen können. 
 Der Agent führt dieselben Schritte durch, die auch ein Mensch durchführen würde: Antrag lesen, Zahlungshistorie prüfen, geltende Regelwerke berücksichtigen, Entscheidung ableiten, Bescheid vorbereiten. Bei Grenzfällen (z.B. zu hoher Betrag, Vorbelastungen, besondere Umstände) übergibt er an eine Sachbearbeiterin. Diese Eskalationslogik ist explizit definiert, nicht dem Zufall überlassen. 
 Der Agent handelt dabei nicht im Vakuum. Er greift auf das Wissen der Verwaltung zu in Form von Prozessmodellen, Entscheidungsregeln oder kommunalen Satzungen. Das sogenannte Company Memory ist eine strukturierte, zentrale Wissensbasis, die KI-Agenten einer Organisation mit demselben institutionellen Kontext versorgt. Ändert sich eine Regelung, kann diese Änderung zentral gepflegt und gezielt an alle Agenten weitergegeben werden ohne jeden Agenten einzeln anpassen zu müssen. 
 Hinweis: Company Memory befindet sich aktuell in einer Closed-Beta Phase. 
 Das ist der Unterschied zwischen einem Agenten, der Aufgaben erledigt, und einem, der sie im Rahmen des geltenden Verwaltungsrechts erledigt. 
 Schritt 4: Der Agent im Einsatz und warum Transparenz keine Kür ist 

 Der Agent läuft. Frau Müller, die um eine Ratenzahlung für ihren Gebührenbescheid gebeten hat, bekommt schneller eine Antwort als je zuvor. 
 Aber was dabei wirklich zählt, ist nicht die Geschwindigkeit. Es ist die Nachvollziehbarkeit. Jede Entscheidung des Agenten ist vollständig dokumentiert: Welche Daten wurden geprüft? Welche Regelgrundlage wurde herangezogen? Warum wurde dem Antrag stattgegeben, oder warum nicht? 
 Im öffentlichen Sektor ist das keine optionale Zusatzleistung. Es ist die rechtliche Voraussetzung für jeden Verwaltungsakt. Und es ist exakt das, was der EU AI Act für KI-Systeme mit Auswirkungen auf natürliche Personen einfordert: Transparenz, Erklärbarkeit, Nachvollziehbarkeit. 
 Der Stundungsantrag ist nur ein Beispiel. Dieselbe Logik gilt für Baugenehmigungen, Sozialleistungen, Vergabeverfahren, Personalvorgänge. Was bleibt, ist immer dieselbe Anforderung: Wenn ein Algorithmus eine Entscheidung vorbereitet, muss jeder Schritt rekonstruierbar sein. 
 Schritt 5: Den Überblick behalten für heute und für morgen 

 Ein Agent ist der Anfang. Die eigentliche Herausforderung beginnt, wenn es zehn werden. Oder zwanzig. Agenten für Forderungen, Genehmigungen, Beschaffung, HR. Jeder mit eigener Logik, eigenen Systemzugriffen, eigenem Verhalten. 
 Der SAP AI Agent Hub ist die Antwort auf genau diese Komplexität: eine herstellerunabhängige Schaltzentrale für alle KI-Agenten einer Organisation. Von hier aus ist auf einen Blick erkennbar, welche Agenten aktiv sind, welche Sprachmodelle sie nutzen, welche Berechtigungen sie haben und ob sie verifiziert und konform sind. 
 Was dabei besonders wichtig ist: Der Agent Hub funktioniert für alle Agenten, unabhängig davon, woher sie kommen. SAP-eigene Agenten, selbst entwickelte Agenten aus Joule Studio, Lösungen von Drittanbietern, alle landen im selben Inventar, alle werden nach denselben Standards bewertet. Ein Rahmen für alles. 
 Das ist Governance, wie sie der EU AI Act einfordert: nicht als Momentaufnahme beim Go-Live, sondern als fortlaufende Praxis mit klaren Zuständigkeiten, Versionierung, Lifecycle-Management von der Einführung bis zur Ablösung. 
 Schritt 6: Den Kreis schließen mit Agent Mining 

 Der letzte Schritt ist der, der am häufigsten vergessen wird und der den Unterschied macht zwischen einem Pilotprojekt und einer nachhaltigen Governance-Praxis. 
 SAP Signavio Agent Mining überträgt die bewährte Logik des Process Mining auf KI-Agenten selbst. Wie verhält sich der Agent im laufenden Betrieb? Welche Entscheidungspfade nimmt er? Hält er sich an die definierten Prozessgrenzen? Gibt es Muster, die auf Regelungslücken hindeuten, oder auf veränderte Rahmenbedingungen, die der Agent noch nicht kennt? 
 Im Fall des Stundungsantrags bedeutet das: Sechs Monate nach dem Go-Live lässt sich datenbasiert beantworten, ob die Bearbeitungszeit tatsächlich gesunken ist, ob der Agent in bestimmten Fällen systematisch eskaliert und ob dieser Befund auf ein Problem in den Entscheidungsregeln oder auf eine Lücke im Company Memory hinweist. 
 Das ist keine Kontrolle um der Kontrolle willen. Es ist die Grundlage dafür, dass KI-Agenten besser werden und dass die Verwaltung bei der nächsten Revision, der nächsten Prüfung, der nächsten politischen Anfrage antworten kann: Ja, wir wissen, was unser Agent tut. Und wir können es belegen. 
 Was das für Ihre Behörde bedeutet 
 Das Szenario mit dem Stundungsantrag ist austauschbar. Was bleibt, ist der Rahmen: Verstehen, wo KI Mehrwert bringt. Bauen, was gebraucht wird mit dem institutionellen Wissen der Verwaltung. Kontrollieren, was im Einsatz ist. Und kontinuierlich lernen, ob die Wirkung der Erwartung entspricht. 
 Die Bausteine dafür sind heute verfügbar. Sie sind so gestaltet, dass sie die Anforderungen des öffentlichen Sektors ernst nehmen: Transparenz, Begründungspflicht, Datenschutz, EU AI Act. 
 Behörden, die diesen Kreislauf heute einführen, schaffen mehr als schnellere Prozesse. Sie zeigen, wie verantwortungsvolle Digitalisierung im öffentlichen Sektor aussieht.

title: Transfer Purchase Orders into the Accrual Engine
author: Ujhelyi_Zsuzsi
text:
Transfer of Purchase Order Items into the Accrual Engine 
 Overview 
 When a purchase order (PO) or PO item is created in Materials Management (MM) (e.g., via transaction ME21N), the system checks whether accruals are applicable. 
 Accrual Object Creation 
 If accruals are relevant, the system generates an accrual (sub)object for the PO or PO item in the Accrual Engine. This can occur in two ways: 
 1. Offline Transfer – After PO creation, existing POs are transferred to the Accrual Engine using transaction POAC_MM2ACE_TRANSFER. 
 2. Online Creation – During PO creation in MM. 
 Note: Accrual objects for POs can be viewed using transaction POACTREE03. 
 Accrual Calculation & Posting 
 Once an accrual object is created: 
 · The Accrual Engine automatically calculates and posts accruals at the end of each period (typically fiscal periods, but other frequencies like days, quarters, or fiscal years are supported). 
 · Optionally, during period-end closing, a manual review of calculated accrual amounts can be performed before posting. 
 · Finally, accruals are posted by executing the periodic accrual posting run as part of the closing process. 
 Offline integration 
 Online integration 
 Steps During Transfer of Purchase Orders into the Accrual Engine 
 During the transfer of purchase orders (both offline and online) into the Accrual Engine, the system performs the following steps: 
 Step 1: Transfer of Purchase Orders into the Accrual Engine Selection of Relevant Purchase Order Items The system identifies purchase order items that require accrual processing. This selection is based on entries defined in the Customizing activity: Define Accrual Item Types and Methods for MM Purchase Order Items → Define accrual item type and method based on PO item. 
 Step 2: Transfer of Purchase Orders into the Accrual Engine: Classify Purchase Order items Algorithm Determination for Accrual Calculation The system classifies the purchase order item to determine the appropriate accrual algorithm. 
 Step 3: Lifetime of an Accrual Subobjects Determination of Start and End of Life Dates The system calculates the accrual period by identifying the Start of Life and End of Life dates, which define the interval for accrual postings. 
 4 Step: Determine Accrual Item Types and Accrual Methods Assignment of Accrual Item Types and Methods Based on the classification, the system assigns the relevant accrual item types and methods (algorithms) to the accrual subobject. 
 Step 5: Create Accrual (Sub)Objects Creation/Update of Accrual Subobject Finally, the system creates or updates the accrual subobject in the Accrual Engine.

text:

 We would appreciate your guidance regarding SAC role design and licensing best practices.

 Test Tenant 
 50 Planning Professional licenses 
 No Planning Standard licenses 
 Production Tenant 
 5 Planning Professional licenses 
 20 Planning Standard licenses 
 Current Design Approach

 Security 
 Editor 
 Viewer 
 Our intention was to transport these roles to Production after validation. 
 Planned Production Model 
 In Production, we are considering assigning licenses as follows: 
 Planning Professional 
 Admin 
 Security 
 Planning Standard 
 Viewer 
 Editor 
 Primary Concern 
 Our main concern is licensing compliance and potential cost impact.

 Questions

title: Advancing Supply Chain Planning: SAP Named a Leader in Multiple 2026 IDC MarketScape Assessments
author: Hagen Heubach
text:
SAP has been named a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for Worldwide Supply Chain Planning Overall Vendor Assessment *. We believe this recognition comes at an important moment for supply chain leaders, as persistent disruption, changing demand, and rapid advances in AI make the connection between planning and execution more critical than ever. 

 Supply chain decisions do not happen in isolation. A change in demand can affect inventory, production, suppliers, logistics, and financial outcomes. The faster conditions change, the more important it becomes to connect those decisions and give people the context they need to act. 

 That is why we are proud of SAP’s recognition across the new IDC MarketScape assessments for supply chain planning. 
 IDC MarketScape vendor analysis model is designed to provide an overview of the competitive fitness of technology and suppliers in a given market. The research methodology utilizes a rigorous scoring methodology based on both qualitative and quantitative criteria that results in a single graphical illustration of each supplier’s position within a given market. The Capabilities score measures supplier product, go-to-market and business execution in the short-term. The Strategy score measures alignment of supplier strategies with customer requirements in a 3-5 year timeframe. Supplier market share is represented by the size of the icons. 

 In addition to the Overall Supply Chain Planning assessment, SAP has been named a Leader in the assessments for Process Industries**, Life Sciences***, Discrete Industries † , and Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) †† . SAP was also named a Major Player in the assessment for Distribution Industries ††† . 

 For us, the breadth of this recognition is meaningful. We believe it reflects the importance of connecting planning to the industry-specific processes, data, and decisions that ultimately determine how well a supply chain responds. 

 Planning has to understand the business 

 Every industry plans differently because every industry operates differently. Life sciences companies need to account for factors such as batches, shelf life, and clinical supply. Discrete manufacturers manage complex bills of material, product configurations, and constrained capacity. CPG companies need to synchronize demand, production, packaging, inventory, and deployment. 
 Enhance decision-making across the supply chain using an AI-enabled planning platform 

 Learn more 

 That business context matters even more as AI becomes part of everyday supply chain decision-making. AI can help planners identify patterns, simulate scenarios, and automate individual tasks—learn more in our AI Buyers’ Guide to Intelligent, Decision-Centric Planning . But isolated intelligence produces isolated value. The bigger opportunity is to apply AI within the context of connected supply chain processes, so a signal in one area can inform what happens next. 

 Microsoft offers one example of what connected, data-driven planning can achieve . Using SAP supply chain planning solutions, the company reduced manual planning processes by 50%, helping its teams minimize inventory and supply chain risk while creating more time to focus on higher-value decisions. 

 Illumina, a global genomics and human health company, provides another example. Using SAP Integrated Business Planning , Illumina achieved a 40% reduction in excess inventory. The company is also applying AI across its supply chain operations as it continues its transformation toward more intelligent planning. Learn more in this ASUG Talks interview. 

 To hear from more customers about how they see AI changing supply chain planning, watch Supply Chain Planning, Reimagined for the Agentic Era . 

 This is also central to how we think about Autonomous Supply Chain Management at SAP . Decision velocity matters, but speed alone is not the objective. Companies need to recognize change, understand its implications, and coordinate the right response based on relevant business context. 

 Connecting planning to action 

 Planning becomes more valuable when companies can act on it. With SAP Integrated Business Planning , companies can connect strategic, tactical, and operational planning across demand, supply, inventory, and response. Those decisions can then connect with processes across manufacturing, warehousing, transportation, business networks, and the broader enterprise. 

 This reflects a larger shift toward supply chain orchestration. As I have written previously , organizations have made significant progress within individual functions, but the opportunity is to connect planning, procurement, manufacturing, logistics, and other processes into a more coordinated operating model. 

 A planning decision may change a production schedule, affecting material availability, warehouse capacity, transportation, and, ultimately, customer commitments. Connecting these processes helps companies understand those downstream impacts and make informed trade-offs based on what is best for the broader supply chain and the business, rather than optimizing one function in isolation. 

 The latest IDC MarketScape results extend beyond planning as well. SAP has also been named a Leader in IDC MarketScape 2026 Warehouse Management assessments for Manufacturing ‡ and Retail ‡‡ . While these are separate assessments, we believe the recognition across planning and warehouse management underscores the importance of connecting decisions across the supply chain. To learn more, read SAP Named a Leader in Two 2026 IDC MarketScapes: Worldwide Warehouse Management for Manufacturing and for Retail . 

 From connected planning to greater autonomy 

 AI is accelerating this shift. At SAP Connect, we introduced new capabilities across Joule Assistants and specialized Joule Agents designed to help supply chain teams sense, analyze, and act across connected processes. The Supply Chain Planning Assistant, for example, is designed to help planners sense, simulate, and resolve exceptions while understanding downstream impacts. 

 This is where we see Autonomous Supply Chain Management becoming practical. The goal is not autonomy for autonomy’s sake. It is to help people spend less time coordinating routine work and resolving exceptions and more time making the decisions that strengthen the business. 

 As AI plays a larger role, trust remains essential. Leaders need the ability to understand decisions, establish guardrails, and maintain accountability. Agentic AI should strengthen human decision-making, giving people the context and intelligence to act with greater confidence while keeping them firmly in control of the decisions that matter most. 

 Turning recognition into customer value 

 We are proud of this recognition from IDC MarketScape, but the real measure of progress is what our customers can accomplish. 

 Our focus is helping supply chain leaders connect planning and execution, build greater agility into their operations, and make informed decisions faster. Increasingly, that means bringing together applications, data, and AI so organizations can move from insight to action across the supply chain. 

 We believe these latest IDC MarketScape results are an important acknowledgment of that direction. More importantly, we believe they reinforce the path we are pursuing with our customers toward more connected, intelligent, and autonomous supply chains. 

 Learn more about SAP supply chain planning solutions . 

 Hagen Heubach is chief marketing officer for SAP Supply Chain Management.

title: GxP Compliance in Life Sciences Is Non-Negotiable: SAP Is Raising the Standard
author: Andre Bechtold
text:
At SAP, our mission has always been to help the world run better and improve people’s lives. Nowhere is that mission more tangible or more consequential than in life sciences. 
 Run resilient operations while accelerating innovation and improving outcomes 

 Learn how 

 Pharmaceutical manufacturers, biotech companies, and medical device makers operate in environments where precision is not a preference; it is a regulatory mandate. Product quality and patient safety depend on it. 

 That commitment has never been static. As life sciences evolve, so does our investment in the capabilities that enable our customers to operate with confidence. 

 Today, one of the most significant expressions of that commitment is SAP’s dedication to delivering a good practice (GxP)-ready public cloud ERP solution. This solution will help ensure that our life sciences and regulated industries customers can bring their most regulated processes into a modern, cloud-based enterprise with the controls, auditability, and validation rigor their industries demand. 

 Why GxP compliance is more critical than ever 

 Supporting GxP across enterprise systems is more critical than ever. GxP is the collective term for all regulatory standards that govern how life sciences companies design, validate, document, and operate systems and processes that can affect product quality or patient safety. 

 As organizations adopt cloud technologies, AI, and advanced manufacturing while operating in increasingly complex global supply chains, the volume of regulated data has grown significantly. Data integrity has become the foundation of GxP compliance, with regulators increasingly expecting organizations to demonstrate that regulated data remains accurate, complete, consistent, attributable, and traceable throughout its life cycle. 

 The scope of GxP compliance has also expanded far beyond the manufacturing floor. Regulated data now moves across cloud platforms, AI tools, business systems, and connected enterprise applications. Compliance must extend across the entire technology landscape, ensuring data integrity, properly governed processes, end-to-end traceability, and confidence in every regulated decision. 

 SAP’s commitment: Extending GxP readiness to the public cloud 

 GxP readiness in SAP’s public cloud ERP is not a feature layered onto a standard product; it is built into every layer of the solution. That means four dimensions of GxP readiness working together: 

 GxP-ready SAP S/4HANA application: Core ERP functionality that customers can validate, providing the documentation, traceability, and audit controls regulated businesses require 

 GxP-ready cloud operations: Managed services and change management processes aligned with GxP expectations for operational integrity and control 

 GxP-ready implementation tools: Accelerators and methodology support for reduced validation effort during deployment and upgrades 

 GxP-ready data centers: A certified infrastructure that meets the physical and logical security requirements of regulated industries

title: Under the hood of a Joule Studio agent: what "Generate Solution" actually produces
author: sergiu_bocancia
text: TL;DR: When Joule Studio generates an agent from a plain-language intent, the result is not a black box you only click through: it is a set of declarative YAML assets (a solution plus agent, MCP server and workflow assets) that deploy as containerized servers speaking open protocols. The agent asset exposes an A2A (Agent2Agent) API with its agent card at /.well-known/agent.json , tools come in over MCP, and the whole solution runs on the SAP-managed runtime of SAP Business AI Platform. In this post I unpack each layer, show the real generated files from the AD164 PoC scaffold, and mark clearly where the documented surface ends and the managed runtime begins.
