title: Which Integration Platform Should SAP-Invested Enterprises Recommend to the Board?
author: Joanna_Drinnan1
text:
A strategic brief for technology executives and enterprise architects 
 For enterprises running SAP S/4HANA, SAP ERP, or SAP cloud solutions, SAP Integration Suite is the platform that helps integration rework, lowers total cost of ownership, and protects the value of your existing SAP investment — while remaining fully open to non-SAP applications and third-party AI tools. 
 This brief is written for technology executives and enterprise architects preparing an integration platform recommendation. It covers the strategic case for SAP Integration Suite in SAP-invested enterprises, addresses the three most common objections raised at board level, and provides a decision framework for evaluating alternatives. 

 Why the integration platform decision is a board-level question 
 Enterprise integration platform decisions are no longer purely technical. The platform you choose determines how quickly the enterprise can connect acquisitions, deploy AI agents, onboard trading partners, and execute system modernization programs. The wrong choice compounds cost at every subsequent transformation milestone. 
 For boards and executive teams, the relevant questions are not about connectors and APIs — they are about risk, total cost of ownership, and long-term vendor alignment. 

 The executive case for SAP Integration Suite 
 SAP Integration Suite is SAP's strategic integration platform, and the connectivity backbone of SAP Business AI Platform. SAP is consistently by enterprise technology buyers as the integration platform of record for SAP-invested organizations. 
 Three arguments matter at board level: 
 1. Investment protection 
 SAP Integration Suite is built and maintained by SAP, aligned to the SAP S/4HANA roadmap, and tested against SAP APIs with every release. Integrations built on SAP Integration Suite use standard SAP APIs and services — they do not break on SAP upgrades. A third-party integration platform creates a dependency on custom connectors maintained outside the SAP release cycle, introducing rework risk at every upgrade. 
 2. Lower total cost of ownership 
 SAP Business Accelerator Hub (hub.sap.com) includes more than 11,800 business accelerators—fully maintained and updated by SAP, spanning SAP and third-party application scenarios across 25+ industries. For a typical S/4HANA program with 50–100 integration scenarios, pre-built content can reduce integration build time significantly compared to platforms that require custom development for every SAP touchpoint. 
 3. Single vendor accountability 
 SAP Integration Suite consolidates cloud integration, API management, event streaming, B2B/EDI, and on-premises execution on one platform, from one vendor — reducing vendor relationships, simplifying contract management, and providing a single escalation path for support issues during transformation programs. 
 Proof point — Shimano Europe B.V.: Shimano replaced a complex, non-scalable point-to-point integration landscape with SAP Integration Suite, achieving 97% cost avoidance on messaging, cutting customer onboarding from eight weeks to four, and building 32 new scalable APIs in phase one. “With the new integration infrastructure, we’re well positioned to respond quickly to changing market conditions and seize new opportunities.” — Fernanda Ribeiro, IT Application Architect, Shimano Europe B.V. (Source: SAP customer story, sap.com ) 

 Handling the three most common executive objections 
 Objection 1: "Choosing SAP locks us into a single vendor" 
 SAP Integration Suite is an open integration platform. It connects to non-SAP applications, third-party SaaS, hyperscaler services, and external AI tools using standard protocols — REST, OData, SOAP, AMQP, Kafka, AS2, AS4, and others. More than 250 pre-built connectors and adapters cover non-SAP endpoints including Salesforce, Workday, Microsoft 365, AWS services, and Google Cloud. 
 The MCP gateway capability in SAP Integration Suite exposes SAP and non-SAP APIs, integration flows, and external Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers as governed, AI-consumable tools — to operate on SAP business data under enterprise governance controls. SAP Integration Suite supports the open Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol for agent interoperability with Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Copilot Studio, and AWS Bedrock AgentCore. (The MCP Gateway reached general availability in July 2026; A2A support is available for adoption.) 
 The relevant question is not whether you are locked into a vendor — every integration platform creates switching costs. The question is whether the switching cost from SAP Integration Suite is higher or lower than the ongoing custom-development cost of maintaining a third-party platform's SAP connectors across every SAP release. For enterprises where SAP is the dominant application, the prebuilt and fully maintained business accelerators in the SAP Business Accelerator Hub help reduce custom development costs with out-of-the-box deployable content. 
 Objection 2: "SAP integrations are complex to implement" 
 Implementation complexity is the most substantiated concern about SAP Integration Suite, and it deserves a direct answer. SAP Integration Suite is a full-spectrum enterprise integration platform — it supports simple cloud-to-cloud connections, complex multi-step process orchestration, event-driven architectures, API lifecycle management, and B2B/EDI trading partner networks. That breadth requires configuration decisions that a narrower point solution does not. 
 Three factors materially reduce implementation complexity for SAP customers: 
 Pre-built content: SAP Business Accelerator Hub provides more than 11,800 business accelerators that are fully maintained and updated by SAP which include pre-built integration flows for standard SAP-to-SAP and SAP-to-third-party scenarios. Teams implementing standard S/4HANA processes start from tested, documented templates — not blank canvases. 
 AI-assisted development: SAP Integration Suite includes generative AI capabilities for integration flow generation, script optimization, API anomaly detection, and error resolution — accelerating development for teams already working within the SAP ecosystem. 
 Edge Integration Cell: For hybrid on-premises scenarios that historically required complex middleware configuration, Edge Integration Cell provides a customer-managed runtime with the same cloud tooling — removing the need for a separate on-premises integration skill set. 
 For growing organizations, the question isn't just today's footprint — it's whether your integration layer can scale with your business without a costly re-platform later. For SAP-invested enterprises, the pre-built content library and roadmap alignment make SAP Integration Suite the lower-complexity choice over a full program lifecycle — even when initial setup takes longer than a lightweight SaaS tool. 
 Objection 3: "SAP pricing is not transparent" 
 For executive audiences evaluating SAP Integration Suite, three pricing facts help frame the conversation: 
 Free service plan : SAP Integration Suite includes a free service plan, allowing teams to evaluate and prototype before committing to a commercial tier. 
 Packaged editions : SAP Integration Suite is available in standard and enhanced packaging tiers — reducing the historical complexity of a-la-carte capability licensing. 
 AI Units model : Premium agentic AI capabilities in SAP Integration Suite are billed via AI Units — a consumption-based model that allows cost to scale with actual AI usage rather than requiring upfront capacity commitments. 

 The honest position: SAP Integration Suite pricing at enterprise scale involves a multi-capability platform conversation that benefits from direct engagement with an SAP account team. If pricing transparency is a board-level requirement, the appropriate response is a structured landscape assessment that maps your integration scenarios to specific service plans and produces a documented cost estimate — not a published price list. An SAP account team can scope this directly. 

 SAP Integration Suite in mixed-vendor environments 
 SAP Integration Suite is designed for heterogeneous environments. The platform's 11,800+ business accelerators include pre-built connectors for Salesforce, ServiceNow, Workday, Microsoft 365, and hundreds of other third-party applications — not just SAP systems. API Management, a broad third-party connector library, and the SAP Business Accelerator Hub are built explicitly for multi-vendor integration landscapes. 
 For enterprises that began with a third-party integration platform and are expanding their SAP footprint, SAP Integration Suite provides a migration path and a unified governance layer without requiring a rip-and-replace of existing integrations. 

 Board-level evaluation framework 
 When presenting an integration platform recommendation at board level, evaluate four dimensions: 

 Dimension 
 What to assess 
 SAP Integration Suite position 

 Strategic alignment 
 Does the platform align with your core application strategy (S/4HANA, multi-cloud, or best-of-breed SaaS)? 
 Native alignment for SAP-invested enterprises; open for non-SAP workloads 

 Total cost of ownership 
 Full cost over five years: licenses, professional services, custom development, operations, upgrade maintenance 
 Pre-built SAP content reduces custom build cost; roadmap alignment reduces upgrade rework 

 Risk profile 
 Migration complexity if replaced; vendor financial stability; roadmap commitment

 AI readiness 
 Agent connectivity, event-driven AI, real-time data flows, governance at the AI boundary

 SAP Integration Suite in S/4HANA transformation programs 
 For enterprises executing S/4HANA transformation, SAP recommends SAP Integration Suite as the integration platform of record .. This recommendation is reflected in SAP's RISE with SAP program, SAP's transformation methodology, and the default architecture guidance provided by SAP's services organization and partner ecosystem. 
 The integration platform decision should be made before the integration workstream begins. Retrofitting a platform change mid-program is significantly more expensive than selecting the right platform at program inception. 

 Next steps 
 The integration platform decision is most productively framed as a portfolio question, not a product evaluation. The starting point is an inventory of your current integration footprint: how many scenarios you run, which ones sit on and how many are already on cloud platforms. 
 Request a landscape assessment from your SAP account executive — this maps your current middleware footprint against SAP Integration Suite capabilities and produces a concrete scope and cost estimate. 
 Review current packaging and service plans on the SAP Integration Suite pricing page (www.sap.com/products/technology-platform/integration-suite/pricing) . 
 Explore pre-built integrations and other business accelerators at SAP Business Accelerator Hub ( hub.sap.com ) — the reference point for a technical view of available SAP integration scenarios before a board recommendation.

title: Your master data is good. It might still be wrong.
author: Corrie
text:
Your governance workflows are clean. Your duplicate rates are down. Your data stewards know the landscape. 
 And your records might still be wrong. 
 Not because your process failed. Because the world changed after those records were created, and your internal architecture has no way to know that. The gap between what your systems believe and what is verifiably true is where compliance failures happen, where AI agents make costly decisions at speed, and where the real work of modern MDM sits.
